# Delivery margin on fixed-price integration work

Revenue on a fixed-price integration is known on day one. Margin is not. Margin
gets decided later, quietly, by how many hours the work actually took — and by
the time it reaches a P&L the engagement is closed and nobody can name the
decision that cost the money.

This model names it.

**All figures are synthetic**, generated by `delivery_margin.py` from a fixed
seed. I have no access to anyone's real engagements.

## The one idea

Unquoted hours all look the same in a timesheet total. They are not the same
problem:

| Cause | What happened | Whose problem |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Quoted work took longer than quoted | Estimating |
| Creep | Work nobody ever quoted | Contracting |
| Rework | The same deliverable built twice | Quality |

Three different fixes. One number hides which one you have. So the bridge runs
margin-as-sold, less scope, less creep, less rework, equals margin-as-delivered,
and it closes to the dollar on every row. The self-check asserts that rather than
me claiming it.

## Run it

```
python3 delivery_margin.py          # writes report.md and engagements.csv
python3 delivery_margin.py --test   # self-check
```

The self-check asserts hours reconcile per row, the margin bridge closes per row
and in total, an engagement with no unquoted hours lands exactly on its target
margin, and commentary is capped and ordered by the money missed.

## What it does not do

It assumes a blended rate. Real delivery has a mix, and a senior engineer on
rework costs more than the average hour this model charges. That understates
rework and overstates scope. Fixing it needs per-person cost, which I do not
have. I would rather name the distortion than hide it behind an average.

It also stops at delivery. It says nothing about whether the engagement should
have been sold at that price, which is the more interesting question and needs
win-rate data.

## Where this comes from

I hold the budget for a finance systems migration at Illumina in Bengaluru, two
cost centres and four projects, moving off IBM Planning Analytics onto OneStream.
The part of that job that transfers is not the tracking. It is having to write
the sentence that explains a variance to someone who will act on it, which
teaches you fast that "spend was higher" is not an answer.
